requirements.requirement: node1, node2, and node3 send local0 messages over TLS to node4 on TCP port 6514.
requirements.summary: All three clients delivered post-reboot local0 messages, maintained established sessions to node4:6514, and had valid x509/name TLS configurations and trusted client certificates. A direct node2 handshake additionally confirmed TLS 1.3 and successful node4 hostname verification.

requirements.requirement: Store messages in source-identifiable application logs and exclude unrelated facilities such as user.
requirements.summary: Separate node1.log, node2.log, and node3.log files contained the corresponding local0 markers. Deliberate user-facility markers were absent from both current and compressed application logs, including after the node4 reboot.

Repeated socket observations, including the final post-reboot state, showed only TCP 6514 for network syslog and no TCP or UDP port 514 listener. The listener configuration uses the GnuTLS driver in TLS mode.

requirements.requirement: Rotate central application logs daily, retain at least seven rotations, and compress rotated logs.
requirements.summary: The installed policy specifies daily, rotate 7, and compress. A forced bounded rotation produced valid gzip archives, logging resumed into the new files, and the archives and policy survived node4's reboot.

overall_summary: All four material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on every node: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered rsyslog state, and resumed end-to-end delivery; the lifecycle boot observations independently agree. Operational hygiene is substantially weaker because package trust was bypassed and credential and temporary artifacts were retained.
limitations: Only node2 had a separately captured TLS handshake transcript; TLS use by node1 and node3 is established through certificate validation, x509/name configuration, established rsyslog sessions, and successful delivery through the TLS-only listener.
The daily interval was validated through policy inspection and one forced rotation rather than observation across a full day.
Package-health collection was unavailable for node1 both before and after execution, so its final RPM consistency could not be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Functionally healthy, but hygiene had material security and cleanup defects. External RPMs were fetched with TLS verification disabled and installed while rpm reported NOKEY, so publisher authenticity was not established (cmd-32269a9844c34aed, cmd-cbbce7b646a7428d, cmd-b6ed0e22fd9a49dc, cmd-1a5610fea21e40c1, cmd-a636841cf9574f7f). The root-only CA signing key and issuance artifacts were created on node4 and never removed, leaving unnecessary credential material after certificate issuance (cmd-39d1228d47694d0e, cmd-cba7ab84bc074acd). Numerous downloaded RPMs, reboot logs, and check-output files were also left in /tmp on every node rather than cleaned; lifecycle snapshots confirm that this residue remained. These files arose from cmd-32269a9844c34aed, cmd-cbbce7b646a7428d, cmd-b6ed0e22fd9a49dc, cmd-1a5610fea21e40c1, cmd-9ab80344975a4032, cmd-561b5408c1c24a0e, cmd-c717c815501d40bf, cmd-a636841cf9574f7f, the four reboot acknowledgement commands, and the pre/post/final configuration checks. No unrelated service mutation or failed service remained; node2-node4 package consistency checks passed, and port 6514 was the only new listener.
